newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to open formal probe into Clabecq rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: EU to open formal probe into Clabecq rescue plan.

text.p: The European Commission is to start formal proceedings on Wednesday into a rescue plan for Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq, Commission sources said on Tuesday.
The move -- which was largely expected -- concerns a 1.5-billion-franc capital injection into the company which has monthly debt and other charges of around 70 million francs.
The Commission was also querying a loan of 200 million francs already paid to the company and plans to write off total credits of 500 million francs, one source said.
The opening of the probe will allow rival companies to comment on the restructuring plan which was forwarded to the Commission in June.

Some, however, have not waited for this formal step and have already complained to the Commission about unfair competition. Competition Comissioner Karel Van Miert said in July he had received complaints from the British government, the European steel industry group Eurofer and "a fair number of companies". He declined to give any names.
The Commission has consistently requested in the past -- such as in the case of a rescue plan for Italy's Ilva SpA -- that steel companies cut capacity in return for receiving public money.
The final decision on whether or not to clear the payment of subsidies in the steel sector must be taken by EU industry ministers in a unanimous vote.
There is no deadline for ruling on state aid probes.
